claim: When an opponent's repeating tax offers 'discard cards or lose life', pay in cards whenever your hand holds surplus lands or duplicates you will never cast. In a pod full of small recurring drains it is the life you hand over voluntarily, not combat, that kills you. Game 0061 turn 19: Obeka, as monarch, took two extra upkeeps and offered 'discard two cards or lose 6' twice; the pilot chose to lose 6 both times, going 40 -> 24, while holding Dimir Aqueduct and a Swamp plus an uncastable Zombie Apocalypse — it ended the game holding two Swamps and Unholy Grotto and had to discard Path of Ancestry to hand size on turn 27. Hearthhull discarded two Forests instead. From 24 the pilot then lost 4 to its own Feed the Swarm, 4 and 6 to Hearthhull's 2-life-per-land-sacrifice drains and 5 to Zuko's Delayed Blast Fireball, reaching 5 life, and Hearthhull's three land sacrifices on turn 28 took it to -1 in round 7 without it ever being attacked for lethal — the 12 life given to Court of Ambition was the margin.
evidence: Game 0061 turn 19: Obeka, as monarch, took two extra upkeeps and offered 'discard two cards or lose 6' twice; the pilot chose to lose 6 both times, going 40 -> 24, while sitting on spare lands — it ended the game holding two Swamps and Unholy Grotto and had to discard Path of Ancestry to hand size on turn 27. Hearthhull discarded two Forests instead. Hearthhull's 2-life-per-land-sacrifice drains then ground the pilot from 24 to 5 and it left the game in round 7 at -1 life without ever being attacked for lethal. (Put right by the fact check: The log's life totals show only 10 of those 19 points came from Hearthhull's land-sacrifice drains. From 24: the pilot's own Feed the Swarm on turn 20 cost 4 (24 -> 20, 'Wilhelt is at 20 life'); Hearthhull's two resolved drains on turn 21 took 4 (20 -> 16); Zuko's Delayed Blast Fireball took 5 on turn 22 ('Wilhelt is at 11 life') and also killed Wilhelt; then drains took 6 in round 6 (11 -> 5, MEASURED 'lost 6 life before its next turn'). Only the final 6 on turn 28 (three land sacrifices) were pure drain, taking 5 -> -1.)

claim: When a spell on the stack will destroy or remove one of your permanents, cash in everything that permanent enables before it resolves: its tap abilities, and every cheap sacrifice you own that its triggers turn into damage or cards. An answer aimed at your engine is a deadline, not a reason to stop.
evidence: Game 0061 turn 26: with Zuko's Damning Verdict on the stack (it killed Mayhem Devil) the pilot first cracked Wooded Foothills and cast Roiling Regrowth, getting two Devil pings plus two Hearthhull drains - Obeka died and Wilhelt and Zuko fell to 5. Turn 21: with Cyclonic Rift targeting Hearthhull it paid {1} and sacrificed a Mountain to Hearthhull's 2+ ability first, drawing two and draining each opponent 2 with counters that were about to be wasted.

claim: When an opponent is already in single digits and the other players are attacking him every turn, let them finish him. Tapping your whole board to take the kill yourself buys you nothing the table was not about to give you, frees the leader's attacks to come at you instead, and marks you as the seat that just removed a player.
evidence: Game 0062: Zuko had been attacked on turns 19 (5 damage), 21 (5) and 23 (11) and was at 11 life with a 4-life-paid, 5-rad-counter board. On turn 24 this seat tapped both its creatures to deal the last 12. On turn 26 Miirym pointed two Scourge of Valkas triggers (7+7) and all four attackers at this seat rather than at Tidus, and it was out on turn 27 while Miirym and Tidus played on for six more turns.

claim: Requests and threat calls only count if you say them to the table on the turn they matter; a plan written in your own notes reaches nobody. Game 0062: after eliminating Zuko on turn 24 this seat had the highest life at the table (40, rising to 41 on turn 25) and a 7/7 flying commander that grew to 9/9 by turn 25, yet its turn-26 note 'Ask Tidus to hit Miirym' was never said aloud — the log shows it never addressed the table, while Tidus did speak to Miirym and spent Path to Exile on Scourge of Valkas.
evidence: Game 0062: after eliminating Zuko on turn 24 this seat had the highest life (41) and a 9/9 flying commander. Its turn-26 note reads 'PRIORITY: survive... Ask Tidus to hit Miirym' — but the log shows it never addressed the table at all (its 14 entries are all private notes), while Tidus did speak to Miirym on turn 26 and spent Path to Exile on Miirym's Scourge of Valkas. Miirym then attacked this seat with everything and killed it on turn 27; Tidus was never asked for anything. (Put right by the fact check: At the end of table turn 24 the seat was at 40 life (HOW THIS SEAT WAS PILOTED: 'round 6 (table turn 24): 40 life', and the only mill that turn was the land Command Tower, so no Glowing One life gain) and Mothman had 4 +1/+1 counters, a 7/7 (turn 22: 'The Wise Mothman now has 4 +1/+1 counter(s)'). The 41 life and the sixth counter (9/9) came later, during Tidus's turn 25.)
